_comment: Provider manifest. It deliberately holds NO list of models: the picker asks each provider what the account can actually use, and a hand-kept list is stale the day the next model ships. What lives here is only what no provider API exposes — prices, and family-level capability rules. Code branches on caps.*, never on a model id.
_capability_note: Rules carry only what the code actually branches on. A context window is NOT here: nothing behavioural reads it, OpenAI does not publish one, and a number written here would be displayed to the user as fact. Where a provider states its own limits (Gemini, Anthropic) they come from the provider and are shown; where it does not, nothing is shown. Rules are matched in order, first hit wins, against the model id. They are written at FAMILY level (^gpt-5, ^gemini-) rather than per model, so a point release inherits its family's capabilities instead of falling back to the conservative unknown-model defaults. Add a narrower rule above a broader one only when a model genuinely differs.
_pricing_note: USD per 1M tokens, indicative only, keyed by exact model id. Providers change prices and expose none of them over the API, so this is hand-kept — a model missing from here simply shows no cost estimate, which is the correct failure. Never guess a price.
